items.title: Howard Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: Bob Stewart and I had him come over to my loft one time and play some stuff for us.

ctx.x: Oh right, on the west coast.

Gerald Wilson. Yeah. And then there was Ray Draper who was just one year older than me but who had several technically, you know as far as playing the instrument, Bob Stewart and I had him come over to my loft one time and play some stuff for us. We found what the problem was, the technical problem. And that was what kept him from getting any farther. He had a beautiful soul thing, you know, that just didn’t come across that well because of the inability to control the instrument and develop some range. But in…
I did not know that. That’s awful. So you moved to New York, how do you find your way into the music community as a newcomer?

items.title: Bob Stewart interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006
items.q: He formed the group Gravity and so not only was I coming in on Friday but I would drive in on Thursday. I wanted to play, you understand? So I would drive that hundred miles from Philadelphia into New York, do a rehearsal

ctx.x: That is a great name by the way. It’s perfect.

He formed the group Gravity and so not only was I coming in on Friday but I would drive in on Thursday. I wanted to play, you understand? So I would drive that hundred miles from Philadelphia into New York, do a rehearsal after teaching all day on Thursday, get back in my car, drive back to Philadelphia, teach on Friday, get back in my car, drive back to New York and do the weekend in New York. I’m very lucky to be here, I’m telling you, because lots of times I would wake up in a different lane. Yeah. I’m very…
I can imagine after, especially the drive on Friday after the Thursday drive and the Friday teaching.
